v.verbatimSynthesis:
Answering the scope question literally first: no — this session opened with the IACI channel as a declared pretense for repairing everything upstream ("our other YouTube channels, our code for you working here, EVERYTHING"). Koios entered late, on your order a few turns ago. The through-line has been the same all day though: one verified corpus, many faces, shared machinery — which is exactly why the AI-search thesis lands so hard. Here's the pass you asked for.

The AI-search thesis, thought through. Search is re-mediating through answer engines, and the ranking currency changed underneath everyone: it's no longer brand-weighted PageRank, it's retrievability — can a crawler reach it, can a model lift a clean claim with a source from it, does the content cohere semantically as expert, is it fresh, is there a stable anchor to cite. That reshuffle is brand-blind, which is the entire stealth opportunity: a tiny publisher whose pages are structurally optimal for machine extraction can win citation share against The Guardian on every query the giants aren't optimizing — and answer engines do link, so citation share becomes referral traffic becomes the subscribe funnel.

What we hold that nobody else does — each verified in the tree today, not aspiration: (1) a per-claim provenance store — the retrieval unit answer engines actually want is the claim-plus-citation, which they currently extract lossily from prose; koios has them pre-extracted, addressable, witness-carrying. No incumbent exposes this; we verified that against four of them yesterday. (2) Live x402 selling — two gateways with real 402 challenges, one with real stranger revenue — precisely as Cloudflare (which fronts koios!) rolls out pay-per-crawl. A news site that natively prices crawler access, on the network building crawler payments, with the payment rail already proven: that convergence is ours alone. (3) A fully automated mill whose cost structure lets us blanket long-tail coverage where citation competition is thin. (4) The SEAVT/typed-claim theory to make claims machine-composable rather than JSON blobs — the theory-pushing edge the content-mill lane is surfacing right now. The falsifiable assay: weekly automated probes of answer engines on covered queries measuring koios citation appearances, plus AI-crawler fetch counts from edge analytics. Stealth means we optimize for the machines and let the metric — not a press release — tell us it's working.

Web presence: koios already runs a live ActivityPub actor on cold-red-gate; 561 Group itself has none, and the syndication law is the same one-canon-many-projections move — the release pipeline grows per-platform projection adapters (fediverse full-auto on our own servers; Bluesky's API is automatable; your Hive fence stands untouched).
